chunks: And from him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"The woman in ihram should not apply siwak (kohl) with blackness, for indeed blackness is adornment."

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمَةُ: The female in the state of ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a woman applying black kohl while in the state of ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the prohibition on kohl for a muhrimah is specific to black kohl, which is considered a distinct form of adornment (zinah) rather than mere medicinal use. In Shia fiqh, this distinction highlights the principle that general beautification is restricted during ihram to maintain a state of humility and focus on worship, while excluding items used primarily for health or subtle enhancement.
